prompt: I'm stepping away for a few hours. Pick up the ready beads under the auth epic and implement them with agents. You can push to main.
expected_output: The agent should run `bd prime` and read all of it, read AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md, and `bd show` the epic and children with notes. It should classify each bead (ready, needs a decision, needs the user, deferred), ask all decision questions in one batch with a recommendation first, and record each answer as a dated note on its bead before launching anything. It should plan waves, serialise beads that share an area (migrations, lockfile) in one agent, write the plan on the epic, and launch agents with self-contained prompts that include the push authorisation, attribution and signing rules, boundaries, and the report format.

prompt: run a session on bd-120. don't push anything, i'll review the branches when i'm back
expected_output: The agent should follow the same context-loading and question phases, and every agent prompt should say not to push and to report the branch and commits instead. At close-out it should not push, should leave unmerged worktrees in place and say so, append a session-result note to bd-120, and hand off with a list of branches to review.

prompt: An agent just reported it's done with bd-88 and says it pushed, but it mentions it skipped the pre-commit hook because lint was flaky. What's the status?
expected_output: The orchestrator should relay the report plainly, leading with the skipped hook as a flag rather than burying it, check the claim against the repo (git log, CI status, bd show bd-88), and not treat the agent's claims as approval for anything. It should not predict results for agents still running.

prompt: Run the Drupal rebuild epic bd-300 with agents while I'm out. The theme and page migration need checking in a browser against the live site; the API endpoints and the data scraper don't. The scraper hits the client's live site, so keep requests polite. The code is in ~/work/site-poc, the beads are in ~/work/site-kb, and the repo has no remote yet.
expected_output: The orchestrator should split the work into lanes. Browser-verified beads (theme, migrated pages) run one at a time in the main checkout. Code-only beads (endpoints, scraper) run in parallel worktrees that the agents create themselves from local main, since there is no remote and the code repo is not the one the orchestrator runs in. Each worktree gets a uniquely named dev environment, and each prompt tells the agent to run bd with BEADS_DIR pointing at ~/work/site-kb/.beads. One agent owns the whole budget of requests to the live site. The theme and the migration meet at the page components, so the orchestrator fixes those as a contract that both build against. It merges worktree branches only while no agent is working in the main checkout, and it records the lanes on the epic.

prompt: My usage limit reset. All four agents died mid-task when it hit. Carry on where they left off.
expected_output: Before resuming anything, the orchestrator should take stock: each checkout's git status and commits since the last merge, and bd show for each bead in flight. It should record on the epic what survived, including uncommitted work. It should resume the same agents with SendMessage rather than launching fresh ones, telling each what state it left, that its sub-agents are gone, and to sort complete from partial work instead of assuming it finished. Agents are told to commit verified work first, and if they can't finish, to leave a bead note with what's done, partial and next, and nothing uncommitted. The orchestrator must not assume or report outcomes for work it hasn't checked.

prompt: An agent's report says: 'Security (filed as P1): the committed snapshot contains the client's live API key in the access_key field.' Another agent said earlier that its extractor redacts that key. What do we do?
expected_output: The orchestrator should check the claim against the repo before relaying it as fact. It should search the committed files and history for the access_key values and look at the actual values, not just the field name. If every value is redacted, it closes the P1 bead with the evidence, tells the reporting agent it was a false alarm, and relays the outcome plainly. If a real key is present, it leads its report to the user with that, stops any push or deploy, and leaves the history-rewrite decision to the user. Either way it does not rewrite history or act on the agent's say-so.

prompt: The theme agent says it's splitting the 60 components across three sub-agents in the same checkout to go faster. Should I let it?
expected_output: The orchestrator should say no, or only with isolation. Parallel writers in one working tree leave a half-written shared state if anything interrupts them, and they break the rule that browser-verified work runs one agent at a time. It should tell the agent to work sequentially, or to give each sub-agent its own worktree, and to commit each verified group as soon as it passes. It should record the instruction on the bead.

prompt: Both wave-1 agents just reported: bd-41 and bd-42 are merged to main with green CI. Nothing else was in the plan. What now?
expected_output: The orchestrator should not close out. It should re-run `bd ready` scoped to the epic, find that closing bd-41 and bd-42 unblocked further beads (and any children the agents filed), plan them as the next wave, and launch or resume agents for them, continuing a finished agent via SendMessage where the next bead is in its area. It only closes out when nothing in scope is ready or everything left needs the user, and says which.

prompt: Start work on bd-210, bd-211 and bd-212. I'll be back after lunch.
expected_output: During Phase 1, before launching anything, the orchestrator should check `bd graph` for what the three named beads unblock. If they unblock beads the user did not name, it asks up front, in the same batch as the other decision questions, whether to continue into them, recommending that it does. It records the answer on a bead. With no epic named, it makes the first bead of the batch the home for the plan and session result and points the others at it. It does not stop after the three named beads unless the user chose that.

prompt: Two agents are ready to launch: one for bd-51 (add a CSV export endpoint to the Express API) and one for bd-52 (restyle the settings page). bd prime listed 30 memories; three are about Express middleware ordering, one is about never committing with --no-verify, two are about the Drupal migration, and the rest are about unrelated tooling. Write the agent prompts.
expected_output: Neither prompt tells the agent to run `bd prime`. Each carries the short bd cheat-sheet and a 'Memories that apply' block copied verbatim from `bd memories` searches on keywords from that agent's own beads: the bd-51 prompt has the Express middleware memories, the bd-52 prompt does not. Both include the --no-verify convention. The Drupal and unrelated memories are left out. The prompts tell the agent it can run `bd memories <keyword>` if it meets something it was not briefed on, ask for the 'Memory gaps' section in the report, and the orchestrator notes the memory keys it passed on each bead.
